result.summary: Escapes backslashes in addition to quotes when formatting the Tor control `AUTHENTICATE` command string. Also adds a functional test case verifying password escaping against the mock Tor control server.
result.problem: When connecting to the Tor control port using `HASHEDPASSWORD` authentication, `bitcoind` formats the password as a quoted string and only escapes quotation marks. Any backslash in `-torpassword` is treated by Tor as an escape character, resulting in authentication failures or malformed commands when backslashes are present.
evidence: PR description: "Tested against Tor 0.4.9.12 with HashedControlPassword set for pa\ss"word\: on master bitcoind logs 'tor: Authentication failed', with this change authentication succeeds and ADD_ONION creates the onion service."
result.scope_notes: Small fix to torcontrol string escaping accompanied by a functional test.
result.card: Escapes backslashes in the Tor control AUTHENTICATE command when using HASHEDPASSWORD authentication. Currently, bitcoind only escapes quotation marks, which causes Tor to interpret backslashes in -torpassword as escape sequences, breaking authentication or malforming the command if the password contains backslashes. The author verified against Tor 0.4.9.12 that passwords containing backslashes fail authentication on master and succeed with this patch.

risk.why: A mistake in string escaping could cause Tor control port authentication to fail, preventing the node from setting up ephemeral onion services.
